primitives.note: Light Binding, Lucent Singularity's cast/detonation, and Final Spark each deal on-cast (or fixed-delay) magic damage on cooldown
Illumination mark, once applied by Q/E/R, is consumed by the next basic attack for bonus on-hit magic damage
the Illumination mark is a binary stack on the dummy applied by any ability hit, refreshed on subsequent hits, and consumed by an attack or Final Spark
Lucent Singularity's slow is a target debuff; irrelevant to damage output itself but listed since it is a defined debuff on the target (no damage amp component, so effectively unused in damage calc)
Lucent Singularity is cast then separately recast/auto-detonates for its damage instance, a second timed part
mana costs (50/60-80/70-110/100) can meaningfully cap casts across a 15s fight depending on mana pool/regen
cooldown starts on cast rather than on detonation (cdstart = on-cast), affecting how soon E can be recast/reused in the window
Prismatic Barrier only shields allies/self; no damage relevance in a solo target-dummy fight

needsBespoke.why: Illumination's mark-and-consume behavior maps to target-stacks (apply/refresh/consume) plus onhit-rider (bonus on-hit damage when consumed by an attack); Final Spark's mark consumption is just an additional consumer of the same target-stacks primitive rather than new logic. Everything else is plain-cast damage or a defensive/irrelevant primitive.

unsettled.question: Is Illumination's bonus on-hit damage available to be triggered by every basic attack against the dummy (once a mark exists), meaning the optimal rotation should attack immediately after each ability lands to consume the mark before the 6s duration or the 0.25s windup-refresh nuance matters, or is there a cap on how often this can proc relative to ability cooldowns?

proposal: Pre-fight: max Q first (or per standard AP mage leveling), start with full mana.
Open with Q (Light Binding) on the dummy to deal magic damage and apply the Illumination mark.
Immediately auto-attack the marked dummy to consume Illumination for bonus on-hit magic damage.
Cast E (Lucent Singularity) on the dummy to deal its impact/zone damage and refresh the Illumination mark.
Auto-attack again to consume the refreshed mark from E.
Recast E as soon as available (respecting its cast-on cooldown) to detonate for its second damage instance and refresh the mark again.
Cast R (Final Spark) when available, both for its own large damage and to consume the current Illumination mark if present (spell shield issues aside).

Continue looping Q on cooldown into an auto-attack to consume the mark, alternating with E's cast/recast cycle and R whenever it comes off cooldown, always inserting an auto-attack after each ability lands to consume Illumination before it can be wasted.
Prioritize spending mana on Q/E on cooldown over auto-attacking without a fresh mark, since auto-attacks without Illumination active contribute only base AD damage.
questions: Should E be recast as fast as possible after landing (near-instant detonation) to front-load damage, or does the fixed 5s duration+recast structure make manual immediate recast always correct regardless of resource cost?
Does R's own damage instance apply a new Illumination mark that a later attack (or R again) could consume, or is R purely a consumer and never an applier?

How many total casts of each ability fit in 15s given cast times (Q/E 0.25s, R 1s) plus attack windups, and does the simulator want attacks interleaved between every ability cast or should abilities be chained back-to-back with fewer attacks in between?

Is base attack speed/AD relevant enough to prioritize weaving multiple attacks, or since Illumination only grants one bonus per mark, is a single attack after each ability sufficient and additional attacks are just base damage?
